title: Agentic Excellence: Mastering AI Agent Evals w/ Azure AI Evaluation SDK — Cedric Vidal, Microsoft
talk_summary: Cedric Vidal demos Azure AI Evaluation SDK/AI Toolkit for evaluating agents: manual spot checks, end-to-end batch runs, automated quality/safety evaluators with thresholds, and JSONL export. The talk is vendor-heavy, but the eval workflow—small manual checks, dataset-based agent evals, and automated scoring—is transferable.

takeaways.what_they_do: Before running automated metrics at scale, manually inspect a few cherry-picked examples side-by-side to understand model behavior and catch obvious issues.
takeaways.evidence_quote: before evaluating at scale you need first to um cherry pick and look at specific examples

takeaways.what_they_do: Run the whole configured agent, including tools/MCP, over a dataset rather than only testing raw model prompts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: once you have selected the model it's time to evaluate it end to end

takeaways.what_they_do: Use automated evaluators that return scores and configure pass/fail thresholds per application risk tolerance.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can configure a threshold. So it's going to get um give you an answer between one and five

takeaways.what_they_do: Export evaluation results to JSONL so they can be reinjected into automated systems for tracking or further analysis.
takeaways.evidence_quote: JSON line file with uh the result of the evaluation that you can then reinject

takeaways.technique: Manual model comparison on same prompt
takeaways.what_they_do: Compare candidate models side-by-side on the same prompt to judge quality and speed before selecting one.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you want to get a clear sense of how different models would respond to a given prompt

takeaways.what_they_do: Build custom evaluators when built-in quality/safety metrics do not match the application’s actual goal.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can also customize and build your own
